messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
You should have just received the first half of the edits. Thank you so much for allowing me the chance to work with your novel. It’s an ambitious and very relevant book. I’ll get into the novel and overview more in the second part of my edits, which will include my 15-20 page editorial letter and a video chat we’ll schedule after you get the letter.

My suggestion is to move through the manuscript and comments not making any changes or edits and just taking the notes in. Then sit with them for a bit thinking about how you want to potentially approach the edits. All my comments are from a perspective of focusing on how to help you meet your intention for the novel and help readers connect with the story and its themes. I would also suggest waiting till getting the editorial letter to make any big changes. The editorial letter will get into more specifics, provide detailed overview of the novel’s elements, break down the movement of the piece, and give more examples and resources to help you as you do your revisions.

Another thing I like to tell authors as they dive into comments along the draft is that there are going to be a lot of sections or moments where I ask questions that are not meant to be answered to me but should be clarified on the page to limit reader confusion and keep the prose and story flowing. All the comments are meant to give you insight into where the story is causing confusion or needs additional work. That all being said, you may do as you like and start editing today! I get that urge. And ultimately this is your novel and I am here to help you.

I also wanted to specify that my comments should not be used to train AI or be fed into an LLM or AI writer to help revise stories or come up with new ones.

If there are specific things you want me to elaborate on or provide additional insight on in the editorial letter, let me know! I’ll be sure to include them. I’ll get into more of your questions and things to pay attention in my letter as well!

Thanks! Talk soon.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Just seeing this. 
I'm on vacation so I will read through the comments and then sit with them. I'll be more focused once I get home anyway. 
I just read through the first few pages and comments. I get what you're saying and look forward to discussing some of this in more detail. Some of the things I did were intentional, but obviously not effective. I can explain when we meet and I see your full notes/letter. This is really helpful because I think I need to find other ways to create a sense of mystery and the unknown. 

We can talk more later, but I know this will be very helpful. Lots of work to do...and questions to ask. :) 

Bela

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: My understanding is that I should read through everything, then approve and pay you? I don't want to keep you on hold, but also want to do this correctly. Let me know. It can move quickly through the comments and if I have questions, I can ask you.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: It is up to you! You can read through all the comments and then approve the work or approve it now. Either way, you can ask questions or ask me to expand on something or in the letter. Approving the work now won't end the contract or our contact and Upwork also auto approves things after a week or 2 whether you do it or not.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Good morning (here on the East Coast),
As I said before, many things you mention (so far) make perfect sense. Things felt off, but I wasn't sure how. Now the big task is HOW to fix them. I've read about half of your comments quickly and as I read, I start to feel - WTF did I write?? I know, normal feelings. You start to question whether it's complete crap, etc. BUT this is good. I haven't had such thorough comments/suggestions and I see now the issues. Moments of rushing, not enough detail...

Now the hard work begins and I'm feeling overwhelmed. Normal, I know. There is the part of me that feels I NEED to get this book out ASAP because it's so important. At at the same time, feeling as if I'll never be able to fix some of the chaos. I feel panic when I think about the TIME it may take. That's just me and my impatience.

Anyway, this is amazing. Your work is exactly what I was looking for and needed. So far, everything makes sense.

I'll be reading through and making notes in a separate document without making major changes. I'm excited. I hope I can do this. LOL.

I'm releasing the payment and will continue reviewing while I wait for your letter.

Talk soon,

Bela

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Let me assure you that your novel is not complete crap! Everything is there. The characters, the world, the story, the emotions, but like you said, now it's time to sharpen them so that your novel has the intended impact you are going for.

All your feelings are normal and valid. It takes time to make a good literary work. If urgency or timing is something that you are concerned about, I can include some publishing guidance in my letter to help you determine what path to publication is right for your novel and intention. Would that be helpful?

I will have the letter finished and back to you by or before 7/20.

I believe you can do this!

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Thank you for your note your note! I understand the moments of fear and needing validation. Although I mostly tell myself that I don't care what people think of my writing, (because I write for myself, in many ways). We are subjective as writers and we may be in love with something we write, but can we ever be objective? Philosophy for 4th.

I don't know whether I will self publish or not. I've self published all my books under my own imprint. I've done my own covers and interior formatting. It's not perfect...but I know how hard it is to get an agent (tried before). AND, I might want more control of my work. I also know how difficult it to market...so, I'm not sure. I'm not in this for money. However, I'd love to make living one day writing. I'm a realist...I have a day job. I do have a short list of small indie presses that I may submit to when the manuscript is ready. If I self publish, I'm hiring a cover designer and interior formatter. Atticus (if you're familiar with it) is limited and not the best.

I've read through the manuscript and I'm still sitting with everything. I decided I'll start taking a deeper look at your comments on Monday after I'm back home. Too hard to focus with crazy but fun family chaos.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Thanks again and enjoy the rest of your weekend!
I have so many typos ha ha
Typing without my glasses is not the best idea. :)

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Good morning (here on the East Coast),

I quickly read through your letter last night and going to take my time and through everything today.

It’s incredibly helpful. Even going through quickly I understood a lot of what you meant.

I can meet almost any time in the afternoon, some mornings are busier for me. If you could, I’d like to meet sooner rather than later. I do have questions about the structure, mostly in the beginning and then would like some clarity on other things you mention.

I think I’ve decided to self-publish. It’s so hard to get an agent, although I do have a couple of indie presses on my list. I did send out some feelers to agents for fun before I had the manuscript edited. Nothing so far, a few nos, but at least rejections took a while. Plus, trad publishing will take forever, I lose control of my work, I still have to do my own marketing... I’d love to hear your take on this. I know how hard it is to get published traditionally and I don’t want to waste time. My book is about my words and my message. Sure, I’d love to make money from it, but that’s not my primary goal. Publishing without an agent, maybe…but it has to be the right place.

Social media is buzzing with data center talk and protests (and AI). I feel something in my gut, but I don’t know if it’s anxiety or excitement. I’d like to get this published as soon as possible – the time is so right. Of course, I want it to be as perfect as possible.

Where do I go from here, once we’re done and I make all of my changes? Is a copyedit enough after this? Money is a bit tight, but I will figure it out. Just need to budget for copyedit, cover, interior format.

Do you have recommendations, particularly a cover designer? Maybe they also do interior formatting. Copyediting will be key, because I’ve added many scenes based on your earlier comments.

I know I’m getting ahead of everything. I feel a pull.

I can meet tomorrow in the afternoon or early evening after 1pm EST, but before 8 pm EST, Thursday and Friday, any time before 4pm EST, Saturday any time after 12pm EST…the following week I am less flexible – can meet Monday between 1pm and 4pm EST, Tuesday anytime.

FYI, I’ve added about 15k words, mostly new scenes, more info about Matt, more details about the world, more character development, esp. for everyone (the men, Sophie). There will be deletions also. That’s one reason why I need to figure out the next editing steps!

You are amazing! Just wanted to tell you that.

Bela

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Hello! Glad to hear you want to meet sooner rather than later. How does Thursday from 1:30 PM to 3 PM EDT/EST work? I'll respond to your questions from your message in that meeting, unless you'd like me to respond in a document and send over the answers.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Replying via email since I'm not on my computer but Thursday 1:30 my time sounds great. 
I can send you a couple of higher-level questions of things I'm thinking about doing and then the other ones we could probably just go through on the call. 
I've been thinking a lot about the beginning of the book, those opening chapters. I have some ideas but I would like to run them by you. 
I'll send a quick summary later about what I'm thinking so you can ponder it before we meet. 
Thank you!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Awesome! We can meet here using Upwork's video meeting feature. I'll keep an eye out for the summary and questions. Looking forward to chatting!

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
I've been sorting through what I want to do with the beginning (first 3 chapters). I like Envoy as the opening, but you're right - his presence in this book is not as the rogue AI. I wanted to introduce him in this book but right now, the beginning doesn't tie in completely.

What if:
Keep it but move it to the end, as sort of an epilogue. Change a few things, so it seems like Sage didn't really shut him down. He was pretending and reboots at the end and it ends with I am God...
What are your thoughts? I have mixed feelings. Is it a lose end, even as epilogue? I also like the way the book currently ends, I think its effective (editing needed). So I'm not sure if that will work. I would love to use the chapter, but not sure how if not at the end.

Regarding chapter 2 (Beginnings):
A) I would delete a big chunk. Change it to 3rd person, so it appears as if someone is telling a story. Then transition to Chapter 3 Mortal Life in some way, to make it clear that the story has now shifted to Sage's perspective. I don't know the most effective to do this or if it makes sense. I would also cut out the first two paragraphs in Mortal LIfe.

B) Delete Beginnings entirely.

Chapter 3 (Mortal Life)
Take the first 2 paragraphs and use it as a prologue (I know how people feel about prologues - mixed opinions), then start the chapter as mentioned above.

I hope this isn't too confusing. I see several options and do really want to keep Mortal Life intact, minus the first 2 paragraphs, delete all of most of Beginnings and possibly change to 3rd person, and move Envoy to the end or sacrifice him :)

I've also been thinking about Sage's childhood voice. I do think it almost sounds like a YA novel. I like the idea of having the voice be who she is in that moment, so we experience the world from her eyes. But need further guidance on this. I do recognize the issues with shifting from story mode (future Sage) to present day Sage and have reworked a lot in the book, except those earlier chapters that I mentioned above.

Happy to hear your thoughts tomorrow!

Some other things we can talk about tomorrow also.

Bela
